transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood SE), Alex (DataHarbor Eng), Priya (DataHarbor PM), Tom (DataHarbor SRE)

Summary (auto):
Quick scoping session to align on benchmark harness integration: customer will run representative scripts through Redwood's harness to validate latency/throughput and cost tradeoffs. Discussed streaming vs non-streaming runs, load profiles, KV/prefix cache behavior, and timeline for running first bench.

Topics: POC success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark harness options (k6/Locust/custom), streaming vs non-streaming, VPC/private deploy constraints, security docs, next steps

Action items (captured): see metadata above

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this to an hour. quick intros?
[00:07] Alex (DataHarbor): hey Alex here, engineering lead, mainly interested in throughput and how streaming affects our realtime product
[00:12] Priya (Product): Priya product, owner of the search assistant feature, success = relevancy plus < 200ms p95 for interactive flows
[00:19] Tom (SRE): Tom, I handle infra and cost -- want to understand unit costs and VPC options
[00:24] Maya: great. daniel and lena from our SE team will cover benchmarking and harness integration. daniel over to you
[00:30] Daniel (Redwood SE): thanks. quick agenda: confirm success criteria, get your workload shape, decide which harness (k6/locust/custom) to plug in, streaming vs non-streaming experiments, and schedule a run.
[00:46] Alex: for workload shape, our production has a mix: 60% short prompts (~30 tokens generated), 30% medium (~150 tokens), 10% long (~800 tokens) for long form summarization. bursts at peak - about 2k rps sustained for 2-3 minutes, 20k rps ephemeral spikes from batch jobs.
[01:06] Daniel: ok that's helpful. quick clarifying q: when you say 2k rps, is that concurrent user queries or token generation rate?
[01:12] Alex: queries/sec. token rates vary but average tokens per request as above, so tokens/sec at peak is higher.
[01:18] Daniel: got it. so we'll model using request distributions and also run token-based throughput tests.
[01:25] Priya: success criteria from product side: p95 latency < 200ms for the interactive paths, end-to-end including network but we understand network is variable. Also quality baselines compared to current model (we'll provide eval prompts).
[01:37] Maya: and from infra / procurement?
[01:40] Tom: we'd like cost targets roughly equal to or better than our current infra bill; also need VPC + KMS for keys and audit logs for compliance.
[01:47] Daniel: in practice we split the POC into 1) benchmark integration - get harness plugged in and reproduce traffic profiles; 2) functionality/quality checks on same prompts; 3) extended soak run to validate caching and evictions. typical timeline 2-3 weeks for first runs.
[02:03] Lena (Redwood SE): on harnesss - we recommend k6 for high-level throughput and locust for custom per-request logic, but we also support customer scripts. If you already have a replay of traffic (traces) we can plug that in and run it deterministically.
[02:18] Alex: we have request traces in protobuf format and a sample of prompt sets. we'll need an adapter?
[02:22] Daniel: yep small adapter; we have examples in our repo. we'll share that.
[02:26] Priya: streaming vs non-streaming - what's the difference for the benchmarks?
[02:30] Daniel: good question. streaming tests measure end-to-end latency for first token (TTFT) and token-per-second tail, whereas non-streaming measures total response latency once the model returns everything. For interactive UIs streaming is usually better UX because first token appears quickly even if total generation takes longer. But streaming often increases the number of small requests to the runtime and changes batching efficiency.
[02:47] Tom: so streaming could increase cost because of fewer tokens per network packet and overhead?
[02:51] Daniel: It can, yes. Overhead per grpc/websocket message and more frequent context switches can lower GPU throughput. But we have streaming-optimized paths and can test both. We'll measure cost per 1M tokens and p95 TTFT.
[03:05] Alex: we also use caching heavily on our prefixes (we often regenerate continuations). how will the harness simulate cache hits?
[03:12] Lena: we'll run two modes: cold start (no cache) and warm start with synthetic prefix reuse to simulate hits. Our harness supports KV cache priming and measuring hit ratios and downstream latency impact.
[03:23] Priya: about metrics - we need p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (requests/s and tokens/s), CPU/GPU utilization, and cost estimate per million tokens. Also observe KV cache hit rate and batch sizes observed.
[03:36] Daniel: noted. we'll produce a dashboard with those metrics.
[03:39] Maya: security and network - Tom you mentioned VPC. are you evaluating Redwood Hosted first or Private?
[03:44] Tom: initial POC can be on hosted but we need to validate VPC and KMS for later stage. Also SOC2 docs upfront.
[03:50] Maya: we will share our SOC2 pack and VPC onboarding checklist.
[03:54] Alex: timeline - we need results by end of month for a roadmap decision. Is that feasible?
[03:58] Daniel: if we start next week and we get traces and prompts within 48 hours, we can run initial streaming vs non-streaming comparison in ~7 business days, then a soak/test for another week. So yes end of month is doable if artifacts are quick.
[04:12] Priya: can we run a short smoke run with a single prompt set to sanity check early?
[04:16] Lena: absolutely. recommended early: 5-10 minute smoke run to validate adapter and instrumentation.
[04:21] Alex: what about model variants and quantization? we may want to test smaller quantized models for cost tradeoffs.
[04:26] Daniel: good point — we'll include a config matrix: recommended baseline model (we'll propose 1-2 open models) plus a quantized variant. We'll measure quality delta using your eval prompts.
[04:36] Tom: any limitations on concurrency per connection? we have clients that open many websockets for streaming, curious about limits and recommended pooling.
[04:44] Daniel: we'll document connection guidelines and recommend connection pooling plus chunked streaming. part of the harness we'll measure concurrency and handshake metrics.
[04:52] Priya: for acceptance, product needs: p95 < 200ms for interactive, quality delta within X% (we'll define), SRE needs cost < current baseline and VPC/KMS validated.
[05:03] Maya: ok will capture as next steps. we'll share the benchmark harness repo and example scripts. also we'll propose three windows for the first load: Tue morning, Thu afternoon, Sat low traffic. which works best?
[05:16] Alex: Thu afternoon or Sat for us. prefer Thu.
[05:20] Daniel: noted. we'll tentatively schedule Thu 2027-01-20 for the full run; smoke run earlier week.
[05:26] Tom: any compliance artifacts you need aside from SOC2/ISO? we might need pen test attestation and audit logs export format
[05:33] Maya: we'll include audit log export examples and discuss pen test scopes with enterprise team; may take longer but not blocking the bench runs.
[05:40] Alex: any gotchas we've seen with streaming tests?
[05:42] Daniel: yes - two common pitfalls: 1) test harness that fires many tiny streaming messages doesn't replicate client aggregation behavior causing pessimistic cost results; 2) not priming KV cache leads to misleading cold-start numbers. We'll help configure client-side simulators that mimic your real client behavior.
[05:59] Priya: on the bench harness, is there an example for our protobuf traces?
[06:02] Lena: yes, we have an adapter template in the repo; we'll send a short README and an example script to convert your traces into k6/locust events.
[06:10] Maya: ok let's recap next steps and owners
[06:13] (brief recap)
[06:15] Maya: 1) Redwood -> share harness repo, adapter examples, SOC2 + VPC checklist by Jan 14 (Maya)
[06:22] Maya: 2) DataHarbor -> export traces and sample prompt sets by Jan 15 (Alex)
[06:27] Maya: 3) Redwood -> prepare streaming vs non-streaming config matrix and proposed model variants by Jan 14 (Daniel)
[06:34] Maya: 4) schedule smoke run early week of Jan 18 and full run Thu Jan 20 (tentative)
[06:40] Priya: sounds good.
[06:42] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll get the traces over.
[06:45] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
[06:49] End of recording
